header.running_head: Hadhrat Umar (RA) Consults with Men of knowledge

blocks.text:
was known as "Radeef". According to the Arabs, a "Radeef" is a person who is regarded as the leader's second-in-command and the term is coined for the one whom the people popularly see as the leader's successor. However, whenever these two men were unable to extract from Hadhrat Umar (RA) the information the people required, they would then send Hadhrat Abbaas (RA).
Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) then asked Hadhrat Umar (RA), "Has any intelligence reached you? What do you intend doing?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) then announced that the people should gather as they do for salaah and when they had assembled around him, he informed them of the latest intelligence. He then waited for their response. Majority of the people echoed that Hadhrat Umar (RA) should march ahead with them in tow. Hadhrat Umar (RA) commended this opinion for he did not like to disregard their opinion. He chose to rather dissuade them in a kind manner. He therefore said, "Prepare yourselves and prepare others. I shall continue with you unless I receive an opinion that is more appropriate."
Hadhrat Umar (RA) then sent for men of insight and the cream of Rasulullaah ﷺ's companions and the most prominent Arab leaders gathered together. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to them, "I feel that I should proceed with the army, but I wish you to give me your opinion on the matter." The men gathered for discussion and unanimously agreed that another companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ should be sent (as commander of the army) while Hadhrat Umar (RA) stayed behind (in Madinah) to dispatch reinforcements. They felt that if victory is achieved, the result would be what everyone desired and if not, another commander and another army could always be sent. In this manner (they said), the Kuffaar would be further enraged, the Muslims would guard against making mistakes and Allaah's assistance would arrive according to His promise.
Hadhrat Umar (RA) then again announced that the people should gather as they do for salaah and they did. Hadhrat Umar (RA) also sent for Hadhrat Ali (RA) whom he had appointed as his deputy in Madinah and for Hadhrat Talha (RA) whom he had sent ahead with the scouting party. At the same time, he also sent for Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) and Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), whom he had appointed as commanders of the two flanks of the army. (When everyone was present,) Hadhrat Umar (RA) then stood amongst the people and said:
"Verily Allaah has gathered the Muslims around Islaam, has created love between their hearts and made them brothers in Islaam. The Muslims are therefore like a single body in their relationship with each other. No part is free from pain when another part is suffering. It is therefore incumbent on the Muslims that their matters be decided by mutual consultation between their men of insight (the consultative assembly). The masses need to follow the one who is their leader and are also bound by the decision of the consultative assembly. The people will have to adopt the course that these men plan.
